question: If a current of 1 A is flowing through a conductor for 10 secs, then the charge flowing through it (in coulombs) will be:
solution:
The Correct answer is __**10 Coulombs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between **current (I)**, **charge (Q)**, and **time (t)** is given by the formula: **I = Q / t**.
 
• Rearranging the formula to calculate charge, we get: **Q = I × t**.
 
• Here, the current (**I**) is **1 A (ampere)** and the time (**t**) is **10 seconds**.
 
• Substituting the values into the formula: **Q = 1 × 10 = 10 Coulombs**.
 
• **Charge** is measured in the unit of **coulombs**, which represents the quantity of electricity transported.
 
• This means that a current of **1 ampere** flowing for **10 seconds** results in a total charge flow of **10 coulombs**.
 
• This calculation is based on the fundamental relationship in **electricity and magnetism**, forming the basis for understanding current flow in circuits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concept of Current:**

 
 
• **Current (I)** is the rate at which charge flows through a conductor.
 
• It is measured in **amperes (A)**, where **1 ampere** represents the flow of **1 coulomb of charge per second.**
 
 
 
• **Charge (Q):**
 
 
• **Charge** is a fundamental property of matter associated with the presence of electrons or protons.
 
• It is measured in **coulombs (C).**
 
• The charge of a single electron is approximately **-1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ coulombs.**
 
 
 
• **Practical Application of Formula:**
 
 
• This formula is used in various fields such as **electronics**, **electrical engineering**, and **physics** to calculate the flow of charge in circuits.
 
• It helps in determining the amount of energy transferred in a circuit over a given time.
